items.title: Offensive and Defensive Rating adjusted for strength of schedule.
items.author: Hoop Informatics
items.body_excerpt:
Offensive and Defensive Rating adjusted for strength of schedule. 

• Higher is better defense
• Farther right is better offense 
• Shaded by net rating 

NBA champions typically finish the regular season top-5 in net rating.

images.alt:
Scatter plot titled "Adjusted Offensive and Defensive Rating," points per 100 possessions, adjusted for strength of schedule, 2026-27 season as of Nov. 21. Each NBA team is shown as its logo. Offensive rating runs along the bottom, with better offense to the right. Defensive rating runs up the side, flipped so better defense is higher. The top right is where you want to be.

The background is shaded by net rating, which is offensive rating minus defensive rating. Diagonal dotted lines mark Net +5, Net 0 and Net -5. Dark teal is +5 or better, light teal is 0 to +5, light pink is 0 to -5, and dark pink is -5 or worse. Gray dashed lines mark the league average on each end, 113.6.

Dark teal, labeled "True Contenders": Spurs +8.8, Celtics +6.9, Thunder +6.3, Rockets +6.2.

Light teal: Timberwolves +4.8, Trail Blazers +4.7, Knicks +4.3, Nuggets +3.3, Pistons +3.1, Grizzlies +3.0, Lakers +2.5, Raptors +1.7, 76ers +1.3, Warriors +1.0, Cavaliers +0.7, Heat +0.3.

Light pink: Suns -0.3, Hawks -0.4, Magic -0.6, Mavericks -0.7, Pacers -1.6, Jazz -3.6, Clippers -4.5.

Dark pink, labeled "Get Ready to Learn Regulation, Buddy": Bulls -5.4, Pelicans -5.7, Wizards -5.7, Hornets -5.7, Kings -8.1, Bucks -8.1, Nets -8.1.

The Rockets have the best offense (118.8) and the Thunder have the best defense (108.2). The Hornets have the worst offense (108.5), and the Nets and Pelicans have the worst defense (118.2).
